hedges.reason: This is the most direct expression of the hedge thesis. The main way C9 fails is that Starmer is replaced and the new Prime Minister moves Mahmood. If Starmer leaves office after a leadership challenge in the second half of 2026, he is also a strong candidate to be the first listed leader out before 2027.

A new Prime Minister or a major reshuffle usually reshapes the great offices together. Moving Mahmood out of the Home Office is often done as a swap with the Foreign Office (Cooper back to the Home Office, Mahmood to the Foreign Office; E10.4 lists Mahmood). A new Foreign Secretary is therefore more likely in exactly the worlds where there is a new Home Secretary.

A full cabinet reset under a new leader, especially a soft-left one bringing back Powell, Haigh or Rayner, would very likely replace Nandy at Culture. This contract pays in the same leadership-change worlds that kill C9.

claims.reason: Mahmood leaving the Home Office would most likely happen in a reshuffle that also rotates the other great offices, either by a new Prime Minister or by Starmer resetting after the May elections. The standard move is a Home Office/Foreign Office swap (Cooper back to the Home Office, Mahmood to the Foreign Office), so a new Home Secretary is likely to come with a new Foreign Secretary.

Starmer put Mahmood in the Home Office only in September 2025 to own migration policy, so he is unlikely to move her himself within a year. The main way a new Home Secretary gets appointed in 2026 is a change of Labour leader and Prime Minister, which means Starmer leaves office. Given the timing, he would probably be the first listed leader out.
